h1: Company culture consulting for small business owners who want a team that runs without them
intro: Things go fine when you're on site. When you're not, corners get cut, people wait for instructions, and good employees leave without saying why. You know culture matters, but nobody ever showed you how to build one on purpose.
definition: Company culture consulting for small business is outside help to define how your team works together and make it stick: a few clear values, regular team meetings, recognition, accountability, and leadership habits that the owner models every week.

sections.h2: Culture is what happens when you're not in the room
paras: Every business has a culture, whether the owner chose it or not. It's how people answer the phone, what they do when a job goes wrong, and whether they speak up or stay quiet.
In a small company, the owner sets most of it, often without noticing. The good news is that culture is built from habits, and habits can be changed.

sections.h2: What company culture consulting for small business covers
bullets: Values: three to five plain statements your team can remember, written in your words, and used when hiring, reviewing and making calls
Weekly team meetings: the same day, time and agenda, so problems surface early and wins get shared
Recognition: simple, specific, regular credit for the behavior you want more of
Accountability: clear owners, clear numbers, and direct conversations when things slip
Leadership habits: how you show up, give feedback and make decisions, because the team copies what you do

sections.h2: How I work with owners on culture
paras: Culture work happens mostly in our owner sessions: four 30-minute calls a month focused on the one or two decisions that matter most right now. Some months that's a hard conversation with a key employee. Other months it's how to run the weekly meeting or what to do about a team member who hits the numbers but drags everyone down.

We start by writing down what you actually value, based on the people you'd hire again in a heartbeat. Then we turn those values into a few routines: a weekly team meeting, a way to recognize good work, and a scorecard so accountability is about numbers, not moods. Between calls, I'm available for support when something comes up.
No posters, no retreats required. Just small habits, repeated until they stick.

For over a decade in banking and finance, I worked with business owners through cash crunches, growing pains and big wins. The teams that held together in hard times had clear values and an owner people trusted. Then I co-founded a company and learned how hard that is to do yourself. faq.q: What does a company culture consultant do for a small business?
faq.a: A company culture consultant helps the owner define a few clear values and turn them into daily habits. That includes weekly team meetings, recognition, accountability and the owner's own leadership habits. The goal is a team that does good work and makes good calls when the owner isn't there.

faq.q: How do I build company culture in a small business?
faq.a: Start by writing down three to five values in plain words, then build routines around them. Hold a weekly team meeting, recognize good work often, and hold people accountable to clear numbers. Hire and correct based on those values. Culture is built through repeated habits, not one-time events.

faq.q: How do I hold employees accountable without micromanaging?
faq.a: Give each person clear ownership of a few results and a number that measures them, then review those numbers weekly. When something slips, talk about it directly and early. Accountability works when expectations are written down, not when the owner checks every task.

faq.q: What are good company values for a small business?
faq.a: Good values are short, specific and true to how your best people already act. Examples include doing what you say you'll do, owning mistakes, and leaving the job site cleaner than you found it. Avoid generic words that nobody can picture in action.

faq.q: How often should a small business hold team meetings?
faq.a: Weekly works for most small teams. Keep it short, on the same day and time, with the same agenda: numbers, priorities, issues and wins. Field crews often add a brief daily huddle before heading out. Consistency matters more than length, so protect the meeting even in busy weeks.
